title: Stroke: history or residual deficits
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's past stroke and any residual deficits.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for residual left-sided hemiparesis.

HPI
The patient is an 89-year-old woman presenting for a follow-up evaluation of her status following a previous ischemic stroke. She reports that she continues to experience functional limitations due to her left-sided hemiparesis. She notes that while she is right-hand dominant, the weakness on her left side makes some activities of daily living more difficult. She denies any recent falls or sudden changes in her neurological status since the last visit.

Medication List
Aspirin 81 mg daily.
Atorvastatin 20 mg daily.

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. She is right-handed and demonstrates functional use of her right side. She exhibits notable left-sided hemiparesis with decreased motor strength in the left upper and lower extremities. No new neurological deficits are noted today.

Assessment
1. Left-sided hemiparesis following a previous ischemic stroke.

Plan
The patient will continue her current regimen of aspirin and atorvastatin for secondary prevention. We will continue to monitor her functional mobility and strength. She was advised to continue with her current physical therapy routine.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, MD
May 14, 2026
explanations: Residual hemiparesis after an ischemic stroke, left non-dominant side: I69.354 (HCC 253).

distractors.why: Check the documented handedness; when it is not documented, the right side is dominant and the left side non-dominant.
Residual hemiparesis is documented: code the sequela (I69.35-, HCC 253), not Z86.73.
